question:
A 2-year-old male is brought to the clinic due to a 5-day history of productive cough. His medical history
includes recurrent lower respiratory tract infections and sinusitis requiring oral antibiotics. He also
experiences frequent loose stools that are difficult to flush. Born at 37 weeks' gestation, his neonatal
course was complicated by meconium ileus. His vaccinations are current. He is at the 15th percentile
for height and the 5th percentile for weight. Vital signs include a temperature of 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse
of 76/min, and respirations of 36/min. Oxygen saturation on room air is 95%. Physical examination
reveals bilateral nasal polyps and scattered inspiratory crackles in the chest. Further diagnostic
evaluation of this patient is most likely to reveal which of the following? Answer Choices: (A) Increased
risk of pseudomonal colonization (B) Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase (C) Hypocalcemia
secondary to vitamin D deficiency (D) Elevated prothrombin time (E) Increased sweat chloride
concentration (F) Decreased residual volume on spirometry (G) Normal coagulation studies (H) Vitamin
A deficiency (I) Metabolic acidosis (J) Decreased fecal elastase levels
 A. Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase
B. Metabolic acidosis
C. Decreased fecal elastase levels
D. Hypocalcemia secondary to vitamin D deficiency
E. Decreased residual volume on spirometry
F. Elevated prothrombin time
G. Vitamin A deficiency
H. Increased risk of pseudomonal colonization

I. Increased sweat chloride concentration
J. Normal coagulation studies
